subject: Acme Health — Private VPC post-call recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Bob Lee <bob.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Acme Health — Private VPC post-call recap

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the time today. Wanted to capture the key takeaways, confirm the constraints you shared, and propose next steps so we’re all aligned.

Recap of pain & goals
- Primary pain: current inference latency and unpredictable costs when processing PHI in the cloud.
- Goal: a private deployment (VPC or on-prem) that keeps inference processing within Acme Health network / approved regions, meets your SOC2/HIPAA requirements, and has predictable per-token cost.

Networking & deployment constraints you mentioned
- No public internet egress from model-serving hosts; all outbound must go through Acme-managed NAT/proxy or be fully isolated (air-gapped option).
- Preferred connectivity: VPC peering or Transit Gateway attachment to our AWS account for cross-account routing; alternatives: Direct Connect with East/West routing.
- Data residency: US-only (patient data cannot leave US regions); optional future EU tenancy for European clinics.
- Key management: customer-managed KMS/HSM required for encryption at rest and in-use key controls.

Compliance & evidence needs
- SOC 2 report and high-level audit scope required for procurement screening.
- Evidence checklist: data retention, access logs, audit trails, and incident response playbook.

Action items / next steps (proposed)
1) Technical deep-dive (networking + security) with your infra team — target week of Nov 30. Proposed owners: Marissa + Priyom from Redwood; Alice + Bob + Acme infra lead.
2) Share sample network diagram and SOC2/evidence checklist — attaching templates in follow-up.
3) Draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with milestones for procurement, security review, and pilot scope.

Please reply with availability for the tech deep-dive and confirm whether VPC peering or Direct Connect is preferred.

Thanks,

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0184
redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-design.pdf, soc2-evidence-checklist.xlsx, mutual-action-plan.docx

From: Bob Lee <bob.lee@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme Health — Private VPC post-call recap

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. Confirming a few items from our side:
- Networking: VPC peering to an Acme-owned AWS account is preferred (Transit Gateway is a second option). Direct Connect would work but adds lead time.
- Air-gap: for our PHI/sensitive clinical imaging pilot, we may require air-gapped (no internet egress) hosts; we want to understand Redwood’s on-prem installer and support model if we go that route.
- KMS: must use Acme-managed KMS; we can provide a dedicated CMK and rotation policy.

Availability: next-week mornings (Dec 1–3) look best for the tech deep-dive.

Also attaching internal note here describing our compliance reviewer’s top concerns (will share formally after they review the SOC2 artifact).

Appreciate the templates — looking forward to the MAP.

Best,
Bob
Head of Infrastructure — Acme Health
bob.lee@acmehealth.com

Bob — thanks for the clarifications. A few quick notes and attachments:

- VPC peering path: we’ll prepare a sample peering diagram and route table checklist for Acme (attached: redwood-private-vpc-design.pdf). That will show options for cross-account peering vs TGW.
- Air-gap/on‑prem: Redwood supports a packaged on-prem deployment (installer + operator runbook). It requires an initial connectivity window for images and a signed installer; after that the environment can be fully isolated. Priyom will cover operational requirements in the tech deep-dive.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed CMKs via AWS KMS and can integrate with your HSM for key wrapping (we’ll include recommended architecture notes).

Attached you’ll find:
- redwood-private-vpc-design.pdf — sample network topologies and routing notes
- soc2-evidence-checklist.xlsx — checklist we use for procurement reviews
- mutual-action-plan.docx — draft MAP with milestones (procurement, security review, pilot, go-live)

Proposed MAP milestones (high level)
- Week 1: Tech deep-dive and initial network design sign-off
- Week 2–3: Security evidence review (SOC2 + checklist)
- Week 4–6: Pilot deploy (VPC peering) and performance validation
- Week 7: Review & decide on air-gap/on-prem pilot if required

Can we lock in Dec 1, 09:00–10:30 PT for the technical deep-dive? I’ll add Marcus (SE manager) and Priyom for the session and share a calendar invite once confirmed.

—
Marissa
